title: The rupee's working lifetime
intro: Early 1980s: one dollar bought about ₹9. Today it costs roughly ₹96 — over 90% of the rupee's dollar value gone in one working lifetime (~44 years).
prompt: What annualized rate of depreciation (% per year) does ₹9 → ₹96 over ~44 years imply?
debrief: (96/9)^(1/44) − 1 ≈ 5.5% a year — quiet, relentless, and almost never discussed: 'most Indian investors have never spent a single evening asking why.' The lesson isn't panic; it's pricing: every long-horizon rupee goal silently carries this leak against globally-priced costs (education abroad, healthcare technology, travel). Hard-currency-linked earning power — exporters in the portfolio, global funds — is the hedge hiding in plain sight, and 5.5%/yr compounding is exactly the kind of number folio's other machines keep showing our intuition underestimates.
